summary.name: LinkLiar
summary.one_liner: LinkLiar is an open-source macOS status menu app, written in Swift, that spoofs the MAC addresses of Wi-Fi and Ethernet interfaces.
use_cases: Hide your MacBook's Wi-Fi identifier from nearby tracking
Change the MAC address of Wi-Fi or Ethernet interfaces without Terminal commands
Build and audit the app from source in Xcode
summary.what_it_does: LinkLiar is a status menu application written in Swift that changes the MAC address of a Mac's Wi-Fi and Ethernet interfaces. The page explains that a MAC address is a unique identifier that nearby parties can use to track a device, and that LinkLiar offers a graphical alternative to the manual ifconfig ether command in Terminal. The author describes the app as open source so its workings can be inspected, and suggests building it from source in Xcode if concerned about administrator privileges. The page also compares it with other macOS tools: Airpass (open source), WiFiSpoof (commercial), MacDaddyX (free), and the command-line SpoofMAC.
notable: Graphical status menu app that replaces manual ifconfig ether commands
Open source, so the code can be inspected and built from source in Xcode
Covers both Wi-Fi and Ethernet interfaces
caveats: Requires administrator privileges to change MAC addresses
Maintained only when the independent developer has time, per the page
